evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692
evidence.field: 日部 entry, printed p. 599 / PDF p. 612; scan pixels directly inspected and matched to supplied source_pixel_sha256. The entry ends on this page; PDF p. 613 (printed p. 600) continues 時, then begins 早.
evidence.text: The 日 entry calls the graph pictographic and says its initial form resembled the sun; it describes later strokes becoming angular, gives sun as the basic meaning, and proposes extensions to sunlight, day, daylight, time, and ruler. These are the author’s explanations; the cited inscription does not establish the order or every semantic transition. In the quoted Shuowen passage, the printed component after 从 looks like 口; the scan alone does not settle its identity against 囗.
evidence.title: 字源

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.field: 形義通解: glyph interpretation and cited oracle-bone and bronze uses
evidence.text: Interprets 日 as a sun image, noting that a round form could be squared because circles were difficult to carve on oracle bones, and that the inner mark distinguished 日 from 囗. Cites oracle-bone examples for sun/sunrise, eclipse, daylight contrasted with evening, a five-day period, and a sacrificial name; it also reports bronze uses for sun, daylight, and calendar-day expressions. These are attested uses reported by the database; they do not establish their relative chronology or semantic links.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：日

evidence.field: Character record: current and historical lexical senses
evidence.text: Lists 日 with senses including sun, daytime, one solar rotation/day, daily, calendar-day unit, and time. Its list supports current Chinese senses sun and day/daytime, but does not on its own establish historical development.
evidence.title: 漢字「日」：基本資料

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, Revised Mandarin Dictionary
evidence.text: Defines 日 rì as the sun, daytime contrasted with night, the time required for Earth to rotate once, daily, and a specific day; it also records Japan as an abbreviation. These support sun/day/daytime as current Chinese senses and show Japan abbreviation is a Chinese dictionary sense, though it is distinct from the basic sun/day account.
evidence.title: 教育部《重編國語辭典修訂本》：日

evidence.field: Exact file description, depiction, source attribution, and reuse terms
evidence.text: The page describes 日-bronze.svg as a modern vector depicting 日 in Western Zhou bronze-script style and cites Xiaoxuetang record 32.EE8F, associated there with 師虎簋 (mid Western Zhou). The Commons page states CC0/public-domain terms for the vector. Its pixels were not visually inspected in this invocation: the direct SVG open failed because the web tool does not render that content type. Do not treat the vessel attribution as proof that the vector exactly matches a particular inscription or infer its mark’s function from the image.
evidence.title: File:日-bronze.svg - Wikimedia Commons

gaps: [SCAN VERIFICATION REQUIRED] 字源, PDF p. 612 / printed p. 599, Shuowen quotation span “从口、一”: the printed enclosure appears 口-shaped, while other consulted transcriptions read 从囗一. The scan was inspected, but its pixels do not settle whether the intended printed graph is 口 or 囗; retain this occurrence as unresolved rather than normalizing it.

The listed oracle-bone examples are catalogued as Shang-period uses by CUHK, but exact dates for individual inscriptions and a sequence among the sun, daylight, day-unit, and sacrificial-name senses were not independently verified. Avoid calling any one use the first-ever sense or inferring semantic transitions from a gloss list.
